I've been working this land for 25 years. I know this soil. My children work in the city now, so it's mostly me and my husband managing the 9.8 mu. We've always done wheat first, then maize — the whole field, every year. That's how it's done here in Quzhou. I don't change what works.

For wheat, I'll plant in October like always. I'll buy Jimai seeds from the village supply store — the same improved variety I've used the last few years. Compound fertilizer goes down at planting, then I top-dress urea at green-up. I'll flood the field from the well three times: once before winter freeze, once at jointing, once at heading. I spray herbicide in spring, and I'll spray again if I see aphids or powdery mildew near flag leaf stage. After maize harvest I'll rotary till to break up the stubble before sowing.

For maize, I sow right after wheat harvest in June — no time to waste. I buy hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or whatever the supply store recommends that's similar. I broadcast compound fertilizer before sowing and topdress urea at the big bell stage. I'll irrigate twice — once if the seedlings look dry, and again at silking when the ears are forming. That's the critical time. I spray herbicide right after emergence. Usually I don't need much else for maize if the season cooperates.

I don't overthink it. My yields are decent. Maybe 450 jin per mu for wheat, 600 for maize. That's always been enough.
